summary.one_liner: OpenJarvis is a local-first framework for building personal AI agents that run on your own devices and call cloud APIs only when necessary.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a Python framework with shared primitives for on-device agents, evaluations that treat energy, FLOPs, latency, and dollar cost as constraints alongside accuracy, and a learning loop that improves models from local trace data. It provides a `jarvis` CLI with a default chat mode, a `jarvis gui` command for a browser chat interface (requires Node.js 22+ from a source checkout), and presets such as morning digest, deep research, code assistant, scheduled monitor, and simple chat. It supports a skills system where skills are tools discovered from a catalog, with import from Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, or GitHub repos, and skill optimization and benchmarking commands. Eight built-in agents are listed across on-demand, scheduled, and continuous modes, including ReAct, CodeAct-style OpenHands, and a monitoring agent with memory. Installers are provided for macOS, Linux, WSL2, and native Windows, and the installer sets up uv, a Python venv, Ollama, and a starter model.
use_cases: run a personal AI assistant locally without sending data to cloud APIs
generate a spoken daily briefing from email and calendar
multi-hop research across local documents with citations
code assistant with file I/O and shell access
scheduled monitoring agent with persistent memory
benchmark and optimize local agent skills from trace history
how_to_run: curl -fsSL <installer URL> | bash  (macOS, Linux, WSL2; exact URL not shown in README)
irm <installer URL> | iex  (native Windows; exact URL not shown in README)
jarvis gui  (graphical browser interface, source checkout, Node.js 22+)
git clone https://github.com/open-jarvis/OpenJarvis && cd OpenJarvis && uv sync --extra dev
notable: Evaluations treat energy, FLOPs, latency, and dollar cost as first-class constraints next to accuracy
Learning loop that improves models using local trace data
Skills follow the agentskills.io open standard and can be imported from Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
One-command installers that set up uv, venv, Ollama, and a starter model
Part of the Intelligence Per Watt research initiative
caveats: Installation notes for WSL2, native Windows service, and desktop prerequisites are deferred to external docs
The GUI requires a source checkout with Node.js 22+; desktop installers are separate release downloads
Larger models and the Rust extension download in the background after install
